visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 stays visually focused on the quadratic roots problem with mostly correct axis/root/parabola representations despite a flawed stacked-equation display, while Lesson 1 spends much of the timeline on unrelated GCD and standard-deviation material and includes several generic or mangled math visuals rather than accurately illustrating the target problem.

interactivity.rationale: Both lessons provide no gate specs or plan JSON, so neither has any functioning checkpoints or input-accepting questions to compare.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 1 provides a clear, coherent narration with spoken math rendered naturally, while Lesson 2 has no available narration transcript at all, making its audio quality impossible to verify and therefore worse on this dimension.

sync.rationale: Lesson 1 lacks beat/cue timing so sync cannot really be verified, but Lesson 2 has no transcript or timing data at all, making it even less assessable on narration-visual alignment.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 correctly applies Vieta’s formulas, uses the root difference to derive roots 2 and 5, and finds k=10, while Lesson 2 has no available transcript or content to demonstrate any correct or pedagogically useful explanation.

polish.rationale: Lesson 1 has larger, more readable typography and a cohesive, polished notebook-style visual design, whereas Lesson 2 is very sparse with tiny left-aligned text, excessive empty space, and some awkward/cropped graph placement despite its consistency.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 1 is the clear overall winner. Although Lesson 2 is stronger on visual accuracy because it stays focused on the quadratic roots problem while Lesson 1 includes unrelated or mangled visuals, the higher-confidence judgments favor Lesson 1 on the most important dimensions: narration quality, concept accuracy, and polish. Lesson 1 has a coherent narration, correctly solves the problem using Vieta’s formulas to get roots 2 and 5 and k=10, and presents a more readable, cohesive design. Sync also slightly favors Lesson 1 because Lesson 2 lacks transcript/timing data entirely. Interactivity is a tie since neither lesson provides functioning checkpoints. Overall, the strong high-confidence wins for Lesson 1 outweigh Lesson 2’s single visual-accuracy advantage.
